@graph.name: Is VOS an OrderEase alternative, and is it better than OrderEase?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not the same thing, and it is worth being plain about it. They manage what happens to orders after they reach you, from however many directions, and VOS changes how one group of customers sends theirs to begin with. At lifting an order out of a kitchen with nobody typing, we think VOS is better. At reading an emailed purchase order, running your EDI partners or wiring up a marketplace, no, and not slightly: we do none of those. If that is the job, buy theirs.

@graph.name: We get a lot of emailed POs. Does VOS read those?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. There is no parser here and we will not imply otherwise. VOS moves accounts off sending a document, which shrinks that pile instead of processing it. For whatever stays on email, their tooling is pointed exactly at it. One limit worth stating: only what comes through the app gets a VOS order number, a timestamp or a stock movement. A call or a voicemail does not.

@graph.name: Does one of them have to go?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not at all, and plenty of distributors would sensibly keep both. They work on separate parts of the same journey: one cuts the queue down, the other handles what is in it. Nothing in VOS has to be removed for your intake tools to carry on.

@graph.name: What about validating orders against our rules?

acceptedAnswer.text: VOS handles it earlier rather than afterwards. A customer can only order lines from their own guide, at the price you set, so there is nothing unrecognized to check later. What VOS does not do is run a rules engine over orders arriving from anywhere else.

They are more open than we are here, and credit where it is due: their site publishes a starting figure and a setup fee, and says there is no free version and no trial. Ours is quote-based, with nothing published at all. Ask us and you will get a number for your own book.

@graph.name: How fast could this be running?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors have this working in 24 to 48 hours, and for most kitchens the first order follows the same day. Nothing is being connected, which is why an OrderEase alternative gets shortlisted by people who have not budgeted for a project at all.

@graph.name: Is it a problem that they are not food specialists?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not on its own, no, and that industry is on their published list. The narrower point is about defaults: a product built to suit eight trades at once starts from generic ordering habits, and a kitchen reordering late at night is not the case it was designed around.
